name: Rula
one_liner: Get matched with an in-network therapist or psychiatric prescriber for video sessions and pay your insurance copay (Rula says about $15 on average).
best_for: People with commercial insurance who want a video therapy appointment soon
People who want therapy and medication management in one practice
Families seeking therapy for children (from age 5) or psychiatry for teens (from 13)
Uninsured people who want a flat, published self-pay rate
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
Uninsured people on a tight budget (self-pay therapy is $150 a session)
People who do not want their data shared with advertising partners
short_description: A virtual group practice of in-network therapists and prescribers; you book a video session and pay your copay or a flat self-pay rate.
long_description: Rula (formerly Path Mental Health) is a US virtual mental health practice whose therapists and psychiatric prescribers work through affiliated medical groups rather than as independent listings. You enter your insurance, answer some questions, choose from matched clinicians and book a video session. Therapy is available from age 5 and psychiatry from age 13 in all 50 states and DC. Rula accepts major commercial plans (including Aetna, Anthem, many Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, Cigna, Optum, Oscar and UnitedHealthcare) and select Medicare Advantage and Medicaid managed care plans in some states. Rula says patients typically pay about $15 a session with insurance; deductible amounts are billed a few weeks later. Self-pay is $150 per individual therapy session, $165 for couples or family sessions, $225 for a psychiatry intake and $175 for a psychiatry follow-up. Missed appointments cost $99 (therapy) or $150 (psychiatry). Rula's privacy policy says it does not sell personal information for money but shares some data with advertising partners for targeted ads.
patient_summary: You check your insurance on Rula, get matched with a licensed therapist or psychiatric prescriber in its group practice, and meet by video. With insurance you pay your copay or coinsurance (Rula says patients typically pay about $15 a session); without coverage therapy is $150 a session and a psychiatry intake is $225.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (Rula says ~$15/session average); $150/session self-pay
pricing.notes: Self-pay: $150 individual therapy, $165 couples or family, $225 psychiatry intake, $175 psychiatry follow-up. Deductible amounts are billed 3–4 weeks after the visit. Missed-appointment fees $99 (therapy) and $150 (psychiatry), not covered by insurance. HSA/FSA accepted.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal information for money but shares some with advertising partners for cross-context (targeted) ads, with an opt-out; you can request deletion (medical and billing records excepted); care records fall under the affiliated medical groups' HIPAA notice.

seo.title: Rula: Flat Per-Session Pay for Therapists & Psychiatrists
seo.meta_description: Rula connects you with licensed therapists and psychiatrists who accept your insurance, with average wait times under 5 days.

faqs.q: How fast can I get an appointment with Rula?
faqs.a: Rula averages under 5 days for first appointments, significantly faster than the typical 6-8 week wait for new patients in traditional settings. Many patients can schedule within 2-3 days depending on availability.

faqs.q: Does Rula offer both therapy and medication?
faqs.a: Yes, Rula offers both licensed therapists and psychiatrists/nurse practitioners. You can receive therapy, medication management, or both depending on your needs. The platform coordinates care if you're seeing multiple providers.
Rula works with most major insurance plans for in-network coverage. The platform verifies your benefits before scheduling. Copays typically range from $0-50/session depending on your plan.

faqs.q: What happened to Path Mental Health?
faqs.a: Path Mental Health rebranded to Rula in 2023. The same platform and mission continue under the new name with expanded services and coverage.

primary_uses: Weekly video therapy with an in-network therapist

availability.note: US only, all 50 states and DC; therapy from age 5, psychiatry from age 13. Select Medicare Advantage and Medicaid managed care plans in some states.
